claims.text: The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026) states Schwab has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, through a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support, today serving more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets.

Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026) describes its goal as providing the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.

Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026) lists Broaden support for RIAs while improving monetization as one of its strategic priorities under Serve More Clients & Deepen Relationships.

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, Advisor Services segment) states its strategy is to maintain its competitive position primarily through the efforts of its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients, plus a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

The 3Q25 transcript (period ended September 30, 2025, Advisor Services) states Schwab is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.
The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026) states Schwab is continuing to invest in the RIA custody business to meet advisers' needs.

The 3Q25 transcript (period ended September 30, 2025, Advisor Services) states that in advisor services Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone, having grown its lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded its institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform to include funds from nearly 60 managers with no transaction fees for clients.

Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published May 14, 2026, Advisor Services) describes its priority as building the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, Advisor Services segment) states it maintains its competitive position primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

Trade press (October 29, 2026) reports Schwab stated it wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, and is increasingly trying to play the role of being their bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.

The 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024, Advisor Services) states that in advisor services Schwab is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

Schwab's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, Advisor Services) states that in the Advisor Services arena Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

Trade press (October 7, 2026) reports Fidelity Investments as Schwab's close rival and the second-largest RIA custodian after Schwab, noting Fidelity offers up to 1.94% on sweep cash and 3.49% through its money market funds.

Trade press (October 28, 2026) notes Fidelity Investments is the second-largest custodian after Schwab, and that Schwab will continue to focus on custody for RIAs under $100 million in assets after Fidelity told such firms they must leave its platform by June 30, 2027.
Trade press (October 7, 2026) reports Altruist, described as the now Vanguard-owned custodian, as a competitor offering 0.05% in sweep accounts and a maximum 3.75% through a high-yield cash account.
Trade press (August 26, 2026) reports Vanguard (through its acquisition of Altruist) as a competitor setting up to compete with Fidelity and Schwab in RIA custody.
A recruiter, quoted in trade press (August 24, 2026), names SEI, Goldman, and Robinhood as other custodians RIAs may look to after Schwab's referral changes.

Trade press (October 29, 2026) reports BNY Pershing named as a custodian alongside Schwab for a breakaway advisory firm, an advisory duo that managed about $18.6 billion in client assets at J.P. Morgan Advisors.
Whole-firm basis, period 2026-09-30: The 3Q26 transcript states Schwab serves more than 16,000 advisory firms on its platform.
Whole-firm basis, period 2026-09-30: The 3Q26 transcript states those advisory firms represent $5.8 trillion in assets.
Whole-firm basis, period 2025: The 3Q26 transcript states that last year more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian, more than 3x the number of the next closest provider.
Whole-firm basis, period 2026-06-30: Schwab's 2Q26 deck reports it ranks #1 in RIA custodial assets at $5.7 trillion.
Whole-firm basis: Schwab's 2026 investor day deck reports 3.9 million households in RIA custodial assets, where it ranks #1.
Whole-firm basis, period 2026Q3: Trade press reports Schwab added 1,001 new RIAs to its custody platform in Q3 2026, with its nearest peers adding 349, 339, 202, and 79, respectively.
Whole-firm basis, period 2026Q3: Schwab's 3Q26 deck reports 1,101 custodians added to ADVs in 3Q26, versus peers at 349, 339, 202, and 79.

Advisor Services segment basis: Schwab's 2026 investor day deck reports $5.2 trillion in client assets in Advisor Services, which it describes as being in a position of strength, and ranks #1 in RIA custodial assets.

Advisor Services segment basis, period 2026-09-30: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services client assets of $5,845.9 billion at September 30, 2026; the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2026-06-30: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services client assets of $5,741.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2026-03-31: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services client assets of $5,201.5 billion at March 31, 2026.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2025-12-31: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services client assets of $5,195.5 billion at December 31, 2025.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2025-09-30: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services client assets of $5,016.7 billion at September 30, 2025.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2026Q3: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services net new assets of $120.1 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Advisor Services segment basis, period 2026Q2: Schwab's press release (October 15, 2026) reports Advisor Services net new assets of $80.2 billion for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

Trade press (October 29, 2026) reports Schwab is pushing to give RIAs equal or better access than wirehouses to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, increasingly trying to play the role of their bank. Why it might matter: the source states Wurster sees pledged asset lines as a particularly fruitful growth area among RIAs, given clients have created enormous wealth on paper from stock positions they don't want to sell but also have everyday liquidity needs.

Trade press (October 28, 2026) reports Schwab made Claude for Financial Advisors available through its central RIA platform and is offering a $4,800 credit for the enterprise version, and also requires RIAs to use Docusign and is partnering with Nevis for digital onboarding. Why it might matter: the source states the $4,800 credit for the enterprise version is offered with the goal of giving smaller advisors access.

The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026) states Schwab collaborated with Anthropic and is the first RIA custodian included in Claude for Financial Advisors. Why it might matter: trade press reports Schwab made Claude for Financial Advisors available through its central RIA platform and is offering a $4,800 credit for the enterprise version to give smaller advisors access.

The 3Q26 transcript (period ended September 30, 2026) states Schwab expects to offer a proprietary long/short investment strategy, extending its direct indexing capability, to deliver long/short capabilities to RIA clients. Why it might matter: Schwab states it will be able to run that product in a very efficient way from a balance sheet and operational standpoint to help sustain the ability to deliver long/short capabilities to clients.

The 1Q26 transcript (period ended March 31, 2026) states Schwab recently launched a structured asset lending program enabling RIA clients to borrow against alternative investments and restricted or private shares. Why it might matter: the source states advisers love the program because historically they had to introduce a big bank for such lending, and now they can keep it with Schwab.

The 3Q25 transcript (period ended September 30, 2025) states Schwab launched Advisor ProDirect, a membership-based program to help independent RIA firms accelerate sustainable growth and support breakaway advisors on their path to independence. Why it might matter: Schwab also recently launched a structured asset lending program enabling RIA clients to borrow against alternative investments and restricted or private shares, extending the support ecosystem for advisors.
